paragraphs: Friend, here is the big idea. The LORD kept reaching for Israel, and Israel kept looking the other way. Hunger, drought, blight and the sword all came, and five times the LORD says, "yet you did not return to Me" (Amos 4:6, 8, 9, 10, 11). I think that line is the heart of this whole passage, because it shows what He was after. He wanted His people back, and He was not only trying to get their attention.

Look at what Israel kept doing in the meantime. They brought sacrifices every morning and tithes every three days, and the LORD says, "that is what you children of Israel love to do" (Amos 4:4-5). They were busy with religion while the poor were being crushed (Amos 4:1). So here is the lesson, baker: a full calendar of religious activity is not the same as returning to the LORD. Amos 4:1 shows the LORD cares how we treat the needy, and that's part of what returning to Him looks like.

Then comes the warning: "prepare to meet your God, O Israel!" (Amos 4:12). And the passage tells you who this God is: He forms the mountains, creates the wind, and strides on the heights of the earth. "The LORD, the God of Hosts, is His name" (Amos 4:13). So ask yourself, friend: where is the LORD calling you back to Him right now? Don't wait for something loud to make you turn. Turn while the ovens are warm and the door is open.
